dedupe_keys.name: nrel industrial process heat demand characterization 2010 to 2015

description: This dataset estimates annual combustion energy use for process heat at individual US industrial facilities from 2010 to 2015, expanding the facility-level process heat survey of McMillan and colleagues from 2015. Facility energy is calculated from emissions reported to the EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program, given in terajoules in total and by fuel type, and further broken down by end use, using the Energy Information Administration's 2010 Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey, and by temperature range, with calculated greenhouse gas emissions in million tonnes of CO2 equivalent by fuel, end use and temperature. It was produced by Colin McMillan and Mark Ruth of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory with Department of Energy funding and published on the DOE Data Explorer on 4 July 2018. Coverage is US facilities that report to the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program. The data are available free through the DOE Data Explorer record; no licence is stated. Caveats: only facilities above the reporting threshold are included, and end-use and temperature splits come from 2010 survey shares, not measurements. For simulation it gives facility-level heat demand by temperature for planning heat supply, electrification and waste heat networks and for testing how fuel supply disruptions affect industrial sites. It is related to the EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program record in this catalogue, its source.
